Atlantic Challenge Mad for Waves

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
Four 21, year old UCT students are en route to make a Guinness World Record- the youngest 4-man team to row, unaided across the 5 500 kms of Atlantic Sea.

Its called the Talisker, Whisky Atlantic Challenge and this is the world’s number one ocean enduro-race and is widely considered to be one of the toughest challenges on our planet, racing across the Atlantic Ocean in nothing but a rowing boat. Fewer people have rowed across the Atlantic than have reached the summit of Everest, journeyed to the North Pole or ventured into space


Further information:
Called MAD 4 waves the team set off from La Gomera, the Canary Islands on the 12th December 2018, a race against 37 other teams to get to Antigua. This is a challenge where experience counts and and ‘youth’ has not in past challenges been an advantage. But in a surprise twist, around the 22nd of January they will be one of the first boats to arrive and embrace the crowds in Antigua… not only are they the youngest team to have ever done this they are coming 3rd in this challenge ( FYI they are coming 3rd in the 4 man teams; 4th in the whole race).

Taking on the extreme challenge of rowing the Atlantic has had its highs and lows; the catalogue of dangers and hardships faced considerable. Sleep deprivation has been a huge issue, for the most part two would row while two slept but some teams have had to have three row while one person sleeps in a bid to get ahead. All their water has had to be desalinated, their meals dehydrated… collision risks, sharks, seasickness, 50 foot waves, chafing (apparently naked rowing is the solution!! interesting for the Go Pro Footage), general wear and tear on the boat especially the rudder.

And what about the psychological strain being confined to a tiny boat with three other people for 40 days with nothing but water as far as the eye can see

A vital part of their on board equipment is 3 Go Pros, so we will not be short of visuals to bring this extreme challenge to life.

These four friends: Cole Barnard, Lee Gordon, Grant Soll and Mathew Boynton have been rowing together for 10 years. In their final, fourth year of varsity they were tantalised by the epic scale of this challenge – could they succeed? To get the boat they took out personal loans, bought the necessary communication equipment, foul weather clothing, safety harness’s etc..

Their charity drives blended together perfectly….rowing for a cleaner ocean – an ocean free of plastics- and supplying of 1 000 plastic recycled school desks to needy rural schools. Each desk uses about 50kgs of plastic to manufacture plastic which might otherwise end up in the ocean. Their campaign has got WWF backing “Rowing for a Cleaner Ocean”.
  
 Team Fact Sheet

Cole Barnard - Nickname: The gardener
From the Mother City, Cole has been passionate about the ocean all his life. Cole is studying Civil Engineering at UCT and if he’s burning the midnight oil, he’s on the water. Cole starred as the lead role in Alibaba’s 2020 Olympics campaign video. Towering with 6 feet 5 inch frame Cole is no strange to leadership, captaining the UCT rowing team for two consecutive years. On this trip Cole brought power to the team and quiet a bit of entertainment as he likes to talk.

Lee Gordon- Nickname: The Cookie Monster – Lee might be a smart cookie but that is not how he got his nickname rather his love of all things sweet… the 40 days of cardboard food tested his sweet tooth.
Lee is in his final year of Chemical engineering. Lee has trained with volunteer wildlife services (VWS) and has been awarded the Presidents award for youth empowerment.
He is happiest when taking things apart seeing what makes them tick and putting them together again, this was a great plus on the boat when wear and tear of constant use of the rowing equipment needed to be fixed, Lee was the one.

Grant Soll : Nickname: The Team Mom. Grant is meticulous, plans ahead and sees that everyone is ok. Grant is studying Chemical Engineering. He has always performed at a high level in Sport winning the SA University men’s 5km time trial. His determination and competiveness was a big factor in the team coming 3rd and breaking a world record. Grant loves music but the rest of the team don’t always like his choice of music – the jury was out on which they preferred, high waves of his music

Mathew Boynton. Nickname: The Boyn-train. Known for being as tough as nails there is nothing that Mathew cant endure, and Mathew is currently doing his Honors in Physics. He has been awarded Springbok colours in Scouts and is fanatical hiker with a passion for adventure.

Press Release:


The Mad 4 Waves Atlantic Challenge
Fewer people have rowed across the Atlantic than have reached the summit of Everest, journeyed to the North Pole or ventured into space. In a 38- to 50-day, 5000km challenge where experience is everything, the MAD 4 WAVES rowing team – four 22-year old university friends – have become the youngest four-man team to row unaided across the Atlantic, even setting a World Record. Carte Blanche meets the youngsters who didn’t shrink back from one of the toughest challenges on the planet.
Producer: Diana Lucas
Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:


Link
Four University friends who have been rowing together since school days
The chance of one last crazy adventure before real life sets in.
Taking on one of the toughest adventures on the planet
And with one small factor none of them had rowed on the Ocean before,

V/O
Lee Gordon
Grant Soll
Cole Barnard
And Mathew Boynton

V/O 13 sec

…took on the Talisker Atlantic Challenge, called the world’s toughest row- where every year teams race across the Atlantic Ocean, unaided.

Derek: Grant their must have been a massive amount of preparation in every way?
Grant: It was a huge obstacle to overcome all of us completing our final year, then you have to go and meet up with a potential sponsor and then you need to go and train and get hours hours on the water so it was this massive juggling act that somehow we a managed to all pull off.

V/O 14 sec
So on on the 12 December they joined 28 teams, seting off from La Gomera, the Canary Islands, their destination Antigua in the Caribbean. An over 5 000 km row of about 40 days.

Cole: It’s a really great vibe and you arrive and your boats been parked nicely in the boat park and there is just a whole line of boats and there is also that bond between you and the other teams because you are about to cross an ocean…
Grant: …you get on to the boat and they call your name to come out to start and you start a rolling start we are all finally ready for it look at each other we are going to do it you start rowing and all you can see is blue ocean and there is no looking back.

V/O 12 sec
Their 8 metre long boat had 2 small cabins and weighed two tons.
The boys rowed two hours shifts on with two hours off to maintain the boat, themselves, to eat and of course sleep.

Derek: When did the body start to take some punishment?
Grant: For me immediately after my second session my knees gave in I was going to do the rest of the crossing without my legs the boat is about 2 tons and I don’t know if I was overexcited the first day and I was using a bit to much oomph.
Lee Grant we are trying to be competitive here and he is not using his legs. LAUGHS
Derek: How much privacy was there?
Lee: Zero none, you have a choice when you went to the toilet do you want to face the guy
Front on, do you want to face him side on …
Grant: You’re on you’re little bucket the waves are going like this you are trying not to spill anywhere.

V/O 3 sec
Cole, was struck drown with seasickness

Derek: You must have felt in the first two week why the hell am I doing this?
Cole: I would say my mental challenge of the row once I got over the sea sickness it became a lot easier. Obviously in the back of your mind WHY am I doing this.

Grant: When you look at documentaries you only hear about the highlights you don’t hear about the four consecutive days you didn’t really speak to anyone you just were in your own head rowing for two hours and you’re trying to go to sleep, too hot and then you’re rowing for two hours again and then it’s just non stop.

Link
In Extreme sports or challenges like this it’s not all about muscle and brawn …but the mind that gives competitors that winning edge….

V/O 6 and a half sec
Mind Coach David Becker works with extreme athletes and had some sessions with the Mad 4 Waves team.

David: Those who have a strong enough WHY will put up with any how and particularly with any endurance events very important when you are doing something for a long period of time over and over again when you are physically mentally and spiritually exhausted to be able to tap into the Why because what I have found that that can be a very powerful and emotional fuel to drive people forward particularly when they are under pressure.

Grant: Our primary goal was to get from A to B safely and our second goal we want to be 4 mates at the end remain friends so no egos on the boat we have got to be there for each other.

Cole…not play blame game was a very big thing for us if something went wrong it wasn’t your problem or his problem it was the boats problem.

Link
Rowing for 15 hours a day expends a lot of energy and the team’s calorie intact was
very important at least 5 000 calories a day all contained in sealed packets packets of not very appetizing dehydrated food

Grant: We were burning 8 000 calories per day and their was no way we could eat 8 000 but we could kind of get to 8 500.
Derek: Did you all lose weight?
Ya, I left Cape Town at 90 and arrived at the finish at 78.

Lee: We came to Christmas and we all put on our little Christmas Hats and Cole and Grant has girlfriends so they got long love letter , Mathew got a big booklet from all his friends with little quotes saying Good Luck Good Luck I hope you are doing well and I got 4 salami sticks and I was completely happy;

Link : And if Christmas had proved a damp squib …New Year was going to be a small but special celebration, with Mathew in charge of the pyrotechnics in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean.

3 2 1 happy New Year …. Woopw
Mathew: we get to the big moment and I pull the ring …
Dude come on
…and nothing
Oh my gosh why isn’t it working

V/O at 5 22
Finally……

Woosh Happy New Year Hey.

V/O 9 sec
The race had a staggered start, so Mad 4 Waves never saw another team and only knew their position from the daily reports on the sat phone…

Lee: It is quite a weird race as you don’t see any competitors but you do know they are their and you do know if they are catching you or not.

Link: After a month of relentless rowing ‘Mad 4 Waves’ had fought to be in third position, a comfortable distance in front of their rivals ‘Row for Victory’ Then a frantic message from home base Row for Victory closing in. It was going to be a fight to the finish

Grant They obviously put a big push on us through the night and we woke and looked at the distance between us and them and we were like hmm
Cole Initially what we did was try to row harder and we found very quickly that that was not the answer, rowing harder meant our backs took a lot of strain so we immediately abandoned that idea.
Grant: Lets try not sleeping because we actually don’t need any sleep.
Lee We were all working hard. No one was sleepy and then you got that sat phone message that they had still put two hours on you…we had to have a little meeting this is becoming a very anxiety filled situation we are not really enjoying the row any more.
Derek: And you can’t see them?
Lee: You can’t see them but you are constantly getting reminded that they are catching you.
Mathew: That was probably the closest we came to having a fall out because it was the last week and there was some differing opinions on what we wanted to have happen YA

Link: After Thirty Nine days of blue sea and sky in the day and occasional showers at night … Cole suddenly spotted a sailing ship in the distance the finish was in sight at long last.
Cole: And there on the horizon I saw tiny little blimp and I was like no guys that cant be Antigua

V/O 14 sec
As they rowed into the English Harbour in Antigua, finishing third in their class Cole, Grant, Lee and Mathew had set a new world record the youngest foursome to have rowed across the Atlantic.

Cole : You row in and everyone is just out on their boats rooting for you it takes you by complete surprise because for the last 39 days you just seen three other faces and you are just overwhelmed and you felt like a rock star.
Mathew: And you land whole things left you speechless… you have forgotten how to walk on land and so you don’t know how to speak you don’t know how to stand .. Grant’s bawling his eyes … LAUGH
Lee You step off the boat and you have 20 camera on you that finish is the best day of my life by far and it would be quiet hard to out do.

It was going to be a fight to the finish Grant They obviously put a big push on us through the night and we woke and looked at the distance between us and them and we were like hmm Cole Initially what we did was try to row harder and we found very quickly that that was not the answer, rowing harder meant our backs took a lot of strain so we immediately abandoned that idea. Grant: Lets try not sleeping because we actually don’t need any sleep. Lee We were all working hard. No one was sleepy and then you got that sat phone message that they had still put two hours on you…we had to have a little meeting this is becoming a very anxiety filled situation we are not really enjoying the row any more. Derek: And you can’t see them? Lee: You can’t see them but you are constantly getting reminded that they are catching you. Mathew: That was probably the closest we came to having a fall out because it was the last week and there was some differing opinions on what we wanted to have happen YA Link: After Thirty Nine days of blue sea and sky in the day and occasional showers at night … Cole suddenly spotted a sailing ship in the distance the finish was in sight at long last. Cole: And there on the horizon I saw tiny little blimp and I was like no guys that cant be Antigua V/O 14 sec As they rowed into the English Harbour in Antigua, finishing third in their class Cole, Grant, Lee and Mathew had set a new world record the youngest foursome to have rowed across the Atlantic. Cole : You row in and everyone is just out on their boats rooting for you it takes you by complete surprise because for the last 39 days you just seen three other faces and you are just overwhelmed and you felt like a rock star. Mathew: And you land whole things left you speechless… you have forgotten how to walk on land and so you don’t know how to speak you don’t know how to stand .. Grant’s bawling his eyes … LAUGH Lee You step off the boat and you have 20 camera on you that finish is the best day of my life by far and it would be quiet hard to out do. BIG ROAR

metadata.Summary: Four 21, year old UCT students are en route to make a Guinness World Record- the youngest 4-man team to row, unaided across the 5 500 kms of Atlantic Sea. Its called the Talisker, Whisky Atlantic Challenge and this is the world’s number one ocean enduro-race and is widely considered to be one of the toughest challenges on our planet, racing across the Atlantic Ocean in nothing but a rowing boat. Fewer people have rowed across the Atlantic than have reached the summit of Everest, journeyed to the North Pole or ventured into space
metadata.Further information: Called MAD 4 waves the team set off from La Gomera, the Canary Islands on the 12th December 2018, a race against 37 other teams to get to Antigua. This is a challenge where experience counts and and ‘youth’ has not in past challenges been an advantage. But in a surprise twist, around the 22nd of January they will be one of the first boats to arrive and embrace the crowds in Antigua… not only are they the youngest team to have ever done this they are coming 3rd in this challenge ( FYI they are coming 3rd in the 4 man teams; 4th in the whole race). Taking on the extreme challenge of rowing the Atlantic has had its highs and lows; the catalogue of dangers and hardships faced considerable. Sleep deprivation has been a huge issue, for the most part two would row while two slept but some teams have had to have three row while one person sleeps in a bid to get ahead. All their water has had to be desalinated, their meals dehydrated… collision risks, sharks, seasickness, 50 foot waves, chafing (apparently naked rowing is the solution!! interesting for the Go Pro Footage), general wear and tear on the boat especially the rudder. And what about the psychological strain being confined to a tiny boat with three other people for 40 days with nothing but water as far as the eye can see A vital part of their on board equipment is 3 Go Pros, so we will not be short of visuals to bring this extreme challenge to life. These four friends: Cole Barnard, Lee Gordon, Grant Soll and Mathew Boynton have been rowing together for 10 years. In their final, fourth year of varsity they were tantalised by the epic scale of this challenge – could they succeed? To get the boat they took out personal loans, bought the necessary communication equipment, foul weather clothing, safety harness’s etc.. Their charity drives blended together perfectly….rowing for a cleaner ocean – an ocean free of plastics- and supplying of 1 000 plastic recycled school desks to needy rural schools. Each desk uses about 50kgs of plastic to manufacture plastic which might otherwise end up in the ocean. Their campaign has got WWF backing “Rowing for a Cleaner Ocean”. Team Fact Sheet Cole Barnard - Nickname: The gardener From the Mother City, Cole has been passionate about the ocean all his life. Cole is studying Civil Engineering at UCT and if he’s burning the midnight oil, he’s on the water. Cole starred as the lead role in Alibaba’s 2020 Olympics campaign video. Towering with 6 feet 5 inch frame Cole is no strange to leadership, captaining the UCT rowing team for two consecutive years. On this trip Cole brought power to the team and quiet a bit of entertainment as he likes to talk. Lee Gordon- Nickname: The Cookie Monster – Lee might be a smart cookie but that is not how he got his nickname rather his love of all things sweet… the 40 days of cardboard food tested his sweet tooth. Lee is in his final year of Chemical engineering. Lee has trained with volunteer wildlife services (VWS) and has been awarded the Presidents award for youth empowerment. He is happiest when taking things apart seeing what makes them tick and putting them together again, this was a great plus on the boat when wear and tear of constant use of the rowing equipment needed to be fixed, Lee was the one. Grant Soll : Nickname: The Team Mom. Grant is meticulous, plans ahead and sees that everyone is ok. Grant is studying Chemical Engineering. He has always performed at a high level in Sport winning the SA University men’s 5km time trial. His determination and competiveness was a big factor in the team coming 3rd and breaking a world record. Grant loves music but the rest of the team don’t always like his choice of music – the jury was out on which they preferred, high waves of his music Mathew Boynton. Nickname: The Boyn-train. Known for being as tough as nails there is nothing that Mathew cant endure, and Mathew is currently doing his Honors in Physics. He has been awarded Springbok colours in Scouts and is fanatical hiker with a passion for adventure.
